shell.practiceExplain: The practice round doesn’t count — it’s just to get the feel.
shell.practiceDoneHint: Now {rounds} real rounds. Your level adjusts as you go.
shell.gradePoor: That was a tough one. Take your time on the next.
shell.levelDown: Level {level} — a little easier, so you can build up again
shell.goodRunHint: {n} more strong rounds to level up

breathing.title: Calm Breathing
breathing.purpose: Slow, steady breathing with a longer out-breath — a calm start before you practise.
breathing.demo1: Press and hold the circle while you breathe in as it grows.
breathing.demo2: Let go and breathe out slowly as it shrinks.
breathing.demo3: Stay in rhythm. Higher levels make the out-breath longer and calmer.
breathing.holdAria: Hold while breathing in, let go while breathing out
breathing.levelHintHold: Breathe in {inS} s · pause {holdS} s · out {outS} s

rotation.title: Mental Object Rotation
rotation.purpose: Turn shapes in your mind’s eye — builds the visual memory you use to picture and remember.
rotation.demo1: Look at the shape and the turn you’re asked to make.
rotation.demo2: Picture it turning, then tap the option that matches.
rotation.demo3: Higher levels: mirror images, bigger shapes and a colour cube.
rotation.whichSame: Which one is the same shape, just turned? (The others are mirror images.)
rotation.explainTurn: {turn} — this is where it ends up.
rotation.explainMatch: Turn the right answer back and it matches. Mirror images can never match by turning.
rotation.cubeRight: Turn the cube a quarter turn to the right
rotation.cubeLeft: Turn the cube a quarter turn to the left
rotation.cubeFlip: Turn the cube upside down (top goes to the bottom)
rotation.whichColour: After turning, which colour is on the {face}?

pictures.title: Picture Memory Sprint
pictures.purpose: Look, remember, recall — trains quick visual memory with everyday pictures.
pictures.demo1: Look at the pictures. You get plenty of time at the start.
pictures.demo2: They disappear. Tap the one you saw.
pictures.demo3: Higher levels: more pictures, less time, and recall in order.
pictures.tapOrder: Tap the {n} pictures in the order you saw them
pictures.levelHintSeen: This level: {n} pictures · {seconds} s to look · which did you see?
pictures.levelHintNotSeen: This level: {n} pictures · {seconds} s to look · which was NOT shown?
pictures.levelHintOrder: This level: {n} pictures one by one · {seconds} s each · recall the order

chunks.dynamicPurpose: Read short passages in word groups at a steady pace — then show what you understood.
chunks.verticalPurpose: Read down a column, one word at a time at first, then in small groups — then check your understanding.
chunks.demo1: The passage slides past. Read the highlighted words.
chunks.demo1Vertical: The passage moves up the column. Read the highlighted words.
chunks.demo2: Then the text hides and you answer a few questions.
chunks.demo3Dynamic: Pick the best one-line summary. Your score is pace × understanding.
chunks.demo3Vertical: Your score is pace × understanding. Groups grow from 1 to 3 words.
chunks.demoQuestion: What do bees show by dancing?
chunks.demoScore: pace × understanding = your effective words per minute
chunks.readyMeta: {words} words · {chunk} at a time · {wpm} words a minute
chunks.readyHint: Read calmly. The text will hide at the end, then a few questions.
chunks.recallOf: Recall {n} of {total} — the text is hidden
chunks.summaryQ: Which line sums up the passage best?
chunks.levelHint: This level: {chunk} word(s) at a time · {wpm} words a minute

eyeBreak.title: Eye relaxation break
eyeBreak.intro: Before reading: look at something far away, then rest your eyes. Skip it any time.
eyeBreak.lookFarHint: Look at something about 6 metres away — out of a window if you can. Blink gently.
eyeBreak.palmingHint: Rest your cupped palms over your closed eyes. Breathe slowly.

glimpse.demo1: Keep your eyes on the dot in the middle.
glimpse.demo3: Then pick what you saw from 4. Higher levels: more items, less time.

span.title: Rapid Visual Span
span.purpose: Take in several things around one point at a glance.
span.demo2: Symbols appear around the dot for a moment.

peripheral.title: Peripheral Flash
peripheral.purpose: Notice what appears at the side while you look at the centre.
peripheral.demo2: A symbol appears near the edge for a moment.

phrase.title: Multi-Word Flash
phrase.purpose: Read a short group of words in one glance.
phrase.demo2: A few words appear for a moment.

blink.title: Blink Recall
blink.purpose: Catch a word that appears for just a blink.
blink.demo2: One word appears for a blink.

focusHub.title: Focus warm-ups
focusHub.intro: Short warm-ups for steady attention before you read. Pick one.
focusHub.schulte: Find the numbers 1 to 25 in order as fast as you can.
focusHub.crossLateral: A side lights up — tap the opposite side.
focusHub.fastPattern: A symbol appears for a moment — pick what you saw.

palace.title: Memory Palace
palace.purpose: Walk through your own home and leave a vivid object at each place — then remember them all.
palace.demo1: Close your eyes and walk through your home with the voice.
palace.demo2: At each place, picture the object big, bright and a little unusual.
palace.demo3: Then pick what you left at each place. You'll be asked again later today and tomorrow.
palace.sameDayIntro: Walk through today's palace once more. What did you leave at each place?
palace.nextDayIntro24: 24-hour recall: what is still waiting at each place?
palace.nextDayIntro48: 48-hour recall: what is still waiting at each place?
palace.nextDayIntroLater: Recall after {days} days: what is still waiting at each place?

fairTest.intro: Read the passage at your normal speed — not faster than usual. Then answer 5 questions. The passage is hidden while you answer.
fairTest.chooseLang: Which language would you like to read in?
fairTest.langNote: Your Day 30 test will be in the same language, so the two results can be compared fairly.
fairTest.doneHint: Scroll to the end of the passage to finish.
fairTest.lowComp: Your comprehension was under 60%. Next time, read for meaning first — speed grows with understanding.
fairTest.tooFastTitle: That was faster than anyone can read with understanding
fairTest.tooFastBody: Your result wasn't saved. Please read a new passage at your normal pace.
fairTest.retakeUsed: You've already used the extra passage. Please message us on WhatsApp and we'll reset your test.
fairTest.oneTimeBody: We now measure reading speed at your own pace. Take this 4-minute test once, so your Day 30 result can be compared fairly with today.
fairTest.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
fairTest.shareText: My reading after 30 days of Sharp Brain: {effective} effective words per minute ({change}).

certificate.title: Certificate of Completion
certificate.completed: has completed all 30 days of {program} on {date}
certificate.readingNote: Words per minute, read at the learner's own pace in {language}. Effective speed = speed × comprehension.
certificate.lockedTitle: Complete Day 30 to unlock your certificate
certificate.lockedBody: Your certificate is ready the moment you finish Day 30's reading test.
certificate.nameTitle: How should your name be printed?
certificate.nameBody: Check the spelling carefully. After this, your name is fixed on the certificate.
certificate.nameInvalid: Please enter your name using letters only (2 to 60 characters).
certificate.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
certificate.cardTitle: Your Sharp Brain certificate is ready
certificate.shareText: I completed 30 days of Sharp Brain with Mind Ur Mind. Verify: {url}

liveClasses.noneUpcoming: No live classes are scheduled yet. Please check again soon.
liveClasses.registered: Registered — Dr. Kapil will send you the Zoom link on WhatsApp.
liveClasses.notEnrolled: Live classes are for Sharp Brain learners.
liveClasses.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
liveClasses.whatsapp: Hello, my name is {name}. I would like to join Class {n} – {topic} ({when}). Email: {email}

memoryCheck.offerBody: A 4-minute memory check, taken once, so you can see how your memory changes by Day 30. It's marked with today's date and your plan day.
memoryCheck.intro: Three short parts, about 4 minutes: remember 20 words, a 10-digit number and 5 people's names. Find a quiet place. There's no time limit for answering.
memoryCheck.chooseLang: Which language would you like the words in?
memoryCheck.otherLangNote: Memory words are in English or Hindi for now. Choose the language you know better — your Day 30 check will use the same one.
memoryCheck.langNote: Your Day 30 check will use the same language, so the two results can be compared fairly.
memoryCheck.wordsHint: The words appear one at a time, 2 seconds each. Just remember them — you'll pick them out later.
memoryCheck.numberHint: The digits appear one at a time. Then type the number.
memoryCheck.facesHint: Each person appears with their name for 5 seconds. Then match each face to its name.
memoryCheck.numberRecallHint: Type as many digits as you remember, in order.
memoryCheck.recallHint: Tap each word you remember seeing. Only tap the ones you're sure about — a wrong tap takes a point away.
memoryCheck.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
memoryCheck.noBaseline: There's no starting check to compare with, so this is your Day 30 result on its own.
memoryCheck.scoreExplain: The average of the three parts.

studio.title: Memory Studio
studio.subtitle: Memory methods you can use for school, work and life. Learn one, practise it, then use it on your own lists.
studio.own: Use it on your own list
studio.ownStorySub: Steps, points of an answer, things to buy
studio.ownPegSub: Reasons, causes, facts — any numbered list
studio.pegsSubRhyme: One picture for each number, 1–10 (they rhyme)
studio.pegsSubShape: One picture for each number, 1–10 (shaped like the number)
studio.nativeNote: Picture names are in English for now — native version coming.
studio.storyDesc: Remember a list in order by linking everything into one funny story.
studio.storyPurpose: Remember a list in order with one linked story.
studio.storyDemo2: Link each item to the next in one funny, moving picture.
studio.storyDemo3: Walk through your story and put the items back in order.
studio.storyStudyTitle: Make one story from these, in this order
studio.storyStudyHint: Link each item to the next: make it big, funny and moving. See it clearly in your mind.
studio.storyWritePlaceholder: A giant rocket lands on a guitar…
studio.recallHint: Tap the items in the order of your story.
studio.suggestLimit: That's all the ideas for today — try your own!
studio.suggestError: Couldn't get an idea just now. Try your own!
studio.suggestNote: That's only a starting idea — change it to make it yours. Your own picture is remembered best.
studio.pegDesc: Remember numbered lists: every number has its own picture, so you can find any item straight away.
studio.pegPurpose: Hang each item on its number's picture, then recall any number.
studio.pegDemo1: Every number has its own picture — a peg.
studio.pegDemo2: Join each item to its peg in one funny picture.
studio.pegDemo3: Asked a number? See its peg, and the item is there.
studio.pegStudyHint: Make one picture: the peg and the item together, doing something.
studio.pegStudyHintHidden: Picture your peg for this number, and join the item to it.
studio.pegLevelHidden: {count} items, mixed order, pegs not shown
studio.pegsIntroRhyme: Each picture rhymes with its number. Say them out loud: one–bun, two–kangaroo …
studio.pegsIntroShape: Each picture looks like its number. Look at the shape: 1 is tall like a candle, 2 curves like a swan …
studio.iceNote: Numbers 11–20 use the same pictures, made of ice.
studio.pegsDone: Well done! Your pegs are now in your review — the first review is tomorrow.
studio.pegsAgain: Almost. Look at the pegs once more, then try again.
studio.ownStoryIntro: Type a list you need to remember in order — the steps of a process, the points of an answer, things to buy. Then make your own story.
studio.ownPegIntro: Type a numbered list you need to remember — reasons, causes, facts. Then join each item to its peg.
studio.listTitlePlaceholder: Causes of the First World War
studio.needStory: Write your story first — even a short one.
studio.tooFew: Add between 2 and 20 items, one per line.
studio.saveError: Couldn't save just now. Please try again.
studio.savedForReview: Saved. It comes back in your review tomorrow, then after 3, 7, 14 and 30 days.
studio.palaceDesc: Remember long lists along a walk through your home.
studio.reviewNone: Nothing to review right now. Items come back 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30 days after you learn them.
studio.pegFront: What is your peg for number {n}?
studio.reviewDoneBody: {remembered} remembered. {forgot} will come back tomorrow for another go.

storyLesson.l1: The Story method helps you remember a list in the right order.
storyLesson.l2: Here is a list: rocket, guitar, tomato, crown, penguin.
storyLesson.l3: Link the first item to the second. A huge rocket crashes into a guitar … and the guitar plays a loud song.
storyLesson.l4: The song is so loud that a giant tomato bursts … splash!
storyLesson.l5: Out of the tomato rolls a shiny golden crown.
storyLesson.l6: A little penguin puts on the crown and waddles like a king.
storyLesson.l7: Now walk the story again: rocket, guitar, tomato, crown, penguin. Each picture brings back the next.
storyLesson.l8: Make your pictures big, funny and moving. Your own story works best — now it’s your turn.

pegLesson.l1: The Peg method helps you remember numbered lists — and find any number straight away.
pegLesson.l2: First you learn ten pegs: one picture for each number, shaped like the number.
pegLesson.l4: 6 – snail. 7 – boomerang. 8 – snowman. 9 – balloon. 10 – bat and ball.
pegLesson.l5: Now hang a list on the pegs. Number 1 is a rocket: picture a rocket taking off from a burning candle.
pegLesson.l6: Number 2 is a guitar: a swan playing the guitar with its long neck.
pegLesson.l7: What was on number 2? Think of the swan … it’s the guitar!
pegLesson.l8: Learn the pegs once, and use them for any list. Let’s learn your pegs.

studio.myPalacesDesc: Build palaces from places you know — your home, school or office, the way you walk — and store long lists in them.
studio.palaceNone: You haven't built a palace yet. Start with your home — you know it best.
studio.palaceStationsHint: These are your stations, in the order you walk past them. Change them to match your own place — every station must be easy to picture.
studio.palaceStationsRule: A palace needs between {min} and {max} stations.
studio.palaceLimit: You can have up to {max} palaces. Edit or delete one first.
studio.palacePurpose: Place one item at each station of your own palace, then walk it again.
studio.palaceDemo1: Walk your palace, station by station.
studio.palaceDemo2: Leave one item at each station — make it big and funny.
studio.palaceDemo3: Walk again: what is at each station?
studio.palaceStudyHint: See the item at this station, as clearly as you can — doing something.
studio.palaceOwnSub: Store a long list along your palace
studio.palaceOwnIntro: Type the list you want to remember. Each item goes to the next station of your palace, in order.
studio.palaceTooMany: Add between 2 items and {max} items (one per station).

palaceLesson.l1: Your own memory palace is a place you know well — your home, your school, or the way you walk every day.
palaceLesson.l2: Choose ten or more stations, in the order you walk past them: the front door, the shoe rack, the sofa …
palaceLesson.l3: Always walk the same way, in the same order. That order keeps your list in order.
palaceLesson.l4: To remember a list, leave one item at each station — and make it big, funny and moving.
palaceLesson.l5: A giant rocket is stuck in your front door. A guitar is playing itself on your shoe rack.
palaceLesson.l6: To remember, walk through your palace in your mind and look at each station.
palaceLesson.l7: You can have up to three palaces: your home, your school or office, and a route.

studio.chapterDesc: Remember the key ideas and structure of a chapter or a book — and walk through them in your own palace.
studio.chapterNewSub: Paste the text or upload a PDF / Word file
studio.chapterNone: No chapters yet. Start with a chapter you are studying now.
studio.chapterNewIntro: Paste a chapter (or upload it). You'll get its 5–9 key ideas and a simple mind map — check and change them, then place them in your palace.
studio.chapterUpload: Upload a PDF, Word or text file (up to 4 MB)
studio.chapterRights: Upload only material you have the right to use for personal study. Your chapters are private to you.
studio.chapterTooLarge: That file is larger than 4 MB. Please upload a smaller file or paste the chapter.
studio.chapterFileType: Please upload a PDF, a Word (.docx) or a text file — or paste the chapter.
studio.chapterUnreadable: The text in this file couldn't be read. Please paste the chapter instead.
studio.chapterGarbled: The text from this file looks scrambled (some older Hindi PDFs use fonts that can't be read). Please paste the chapter text instead.
studio.chapterTooShort: Please add more of the chapter — at least about 120 words.
studio.chapterLimit: You've made 3 new chapters today — that's the daily limit. Your saved chapters are always open.
studio.chapterUnavailable: Couldn't make the key ideas just now. Please try again in a minute.
studio.chapterEditHint: These are suggestions — change any idea to your own words, put them in the order you want, delete or add ideas.
studio.ideasRule: Keep between {min} and {max} ideas, each with a title.
studio.chapterPalace: Where will you place these ideas?
studio.chapterDefaultWalk: A walk through a home (suggested stations)
studio.chapterStartJourney: Save and start the chapter journey
studio.chapterJourneyHint: Picture this idea at {station}: make it big, funny and moving, so the station brings the idea back.
studio.chapterWeak: These ideas come back in your review tomorrow:
studio.chapterAllRight: You recalled every idea. The chapter comes back in your review tomorrow.

chapterLesson.l1: Chapter and Book helps you remember the key ideas of a chapter — and how they fit together.
chapterLesson.l2: First, paste or upload the chapter. The app suggests its five to nine key ideas and a simple mind map.
chapterLesson.l3: Check them. Change any idea to your own words, and keep the ideas in the order of the chapter.
chapterLesson.l4: Then place the ideas in your memory palace — one idea at each station, in order.
chapterLesson.l5: At each station, make one vivid picture that joins the place and the idea.
chapterLesson.l6: A whole book works the same way: the book is a building, and each chapter is a room in it.
chapterLesson.l7: Now walk the chapter: go through your palace and say each idea. Then answer five questions.
chapterLesson.l8: Ideas you miss come back in your review. Let's start with a chapter you are studying now.

studio.nameFaceDesc: Remember the name of every new person you meet — in class, at work, at a wedding.
studio.facePurpose: Notice one feature, turn the name into a picture, and link the two.
studio.faceDemo1: Look at the face: notice one thing that stands out.
studio.faceDemo2: Turn the name into a picture — Kiran means a ray of light.
studio.faceDemo3: See the faces again in a new order: who is who?
studio.faceStudyHint: Turn the name into a picture and join it to what you noticed. Say the name once in your mind.
studio.faceWritePlaceholder: Rays of light shining out of the glasses…
studio.faceOwnSub: A new class, a new office, relatives at a wedding
studio.faceOwnIntro: Write the names of people you have met, who they are and what stands out about them. Only words are saved — never a photo.
studio.faceOwnWho: Who they are and what stands out (tall, maths teacher…)
studio.faceOwnPrivacy: Your lists are private to you.
studio.faceOwnNeedWho: For each person, write who they are or what stands out.

nameFaceLesson.l1: Names and faces helps you remember the name of every new person you meet.
nameFaceLesson.l2: First, look at the face and notice one thing that stands out. Here: round glasses.
nameFaceLesson.l3: Next, turn the name into a picture. This is Kiran — and kiran means a ray of light.
nameFaceLesson.l4: Many names have a meaning you can picture: Akash is the sky, Neel is blue, Pankaj is a lotus. For other names, use a word that sounds like the name.
nameFaceLesson.l5: Now join the two: picture bright rays of light shining out of Kiran's round glasses.
nameFaceLesson.l6: Make the picture big, funny and moving — and say the name once in your mind.
nameFaceLesson.l7: When you see the face again, the glasses bring back the rays of light, and the light brings back the name: Kiran.
nameFaceLesson.l8: Let's practise. First two faces, then three.

studio.numberDesc: Remember numbers, dates and formulas: every pair of digits from 00 to 99 has its own picture.
studio.numberPurpose: Turn the number into pictures, make one scene, then type the number back.
studio.numberDemo1: Split the number into pairs of digits.
studio.numberDemo2: Each pair has its picture — make one funny scene with them, in order.
studio.numberDemo3: Walk through your scene and read the number back.
studio.numberCardHint: Say the number and the word aloud, and see the picture clearly. The sounds of the word give the number.
studio.numberSetDone: Well done! These 10 pictures are now in your review — the first review is tomorrow.
studio.numberSetsIntro: Learn the 100 pictures 10 at a time — one set a day is plenty. A tick shows the sets you have learned.
studio.numberNoPictures: Turn each pair into its picture in your mind.
studio.numberStudyHint: Make one scene with the pictures, in order — big, funny and moving.
studio.numberDateHint: Make one scene: the event with the two pictures in it.
studio.numberOwnRule: Add at least 2 numbers, each with a name and at least 2 digits.
studio.numberOwnIntro: Add numbers you need to remember — a formula's constant, a date, a roll number. Each one appears as its pictures.
studio.numberOwnLabel: What is it? (e.g. speed of light in km/s)
studio.numberOwnPrivacy: Never save passwords, PINs or bank numbers. Your lists are private to you.
studio.numberDatesSub: Remember the year of an event with one scene

numberLessonEn.l1: Number pictures turn numbers that are hard to remember into pictures you can see.
numberLessonEn.l2: Every digit has a sound. 0 is s, 1 is t or d, 2 is n, 3 is m, and 4 is r.
numberLessonEn.l3: 5 is l, 6 is j, ch or sh, 7 is k or g, 8 is f or v, and 9 is p or b.
numberLessonEn.l4: Two digits make a word from their sounds. 4 and 7 — r and k — a raccoon. 1 and 9 — t and p — a tap.
numberLessonEn.l5: Vowels don't count, and only the first two sounds matter. You learn one hundred pictures, ten at a time.
numberLessonEn.l6: Now the number 4719. Split it into pairs: 47 and 19 — a raccoon and a tap.
numberLessonEn.l7: Make one funny scene: a raccoon washing its paws under a tap, splashing everywhere. Read it back: raccoon, tap — 4 7 1 9.
numberLessonEn.l8: Start with the first ten pictures, 00 to 09.

numberLessonHi.l1: अंकों की तस्वीरें मुश्किल संख्याओं को ऐसी तस्वीरों में बदल देती हैं जिन्हें आप देख सकते हैं।
numberLessonHi.l2: हर अंक की एक आवाज़ है। 0 = स, 1 = त, द, ट या ड, 2 = न, 3 = म, और 4 = र या ड़।
numberLessonHi.l3: 5 = ल, 6 = च, ज या श, 7 = क या ग, 8 = फ या व, और 9 = प, ब या भ।
numberLessonHi.l4: दो अंक अपनी आवाज़ों से एक शब्द बनाते हैं। 4 और 7 — र और ख — राखी। 2 और 5 — न और ल — नल।
numberLessonHi.l5: मात्राएँ नहीं गिनी जातीं, सिर्फ़ पहली दो आवाज़ें गिनी जाती हैं। आप सौ तस्वीरें सीखते हैं, दस-दस करके।
numberLessonHi.l6: अब संख्या 4725। इसे जोड़ों में बाँटिए: 47 और 25 — राखी और नल।
numberLessonHi.l7: एक मज़ेदार दृश्य बनाइए: नल से पानी की जगह राखियाँ निकल रही हैं! फिर उल्टा पढ़िए: राखी, नल — 4 7 2 5।
numberLessonHi.l8: पहली दस तस्वीरों से शुरू कीजिए: 00 से 09 तक।

studio.keywordDesc: Learn new words — English words, science terms, another language — with a sound-alike word and one picture.
studio.keywordPurpose: Find a word that sounds like the new word, and join it to the meaning in one picture.
studio.keywordDemo1: A new word and its meaning.
studio.keywordDemo2: A keyword: a word you know that sounds like it.
studio.keywordDemo3: One picture that joins the keyword and the meaning.
studio.keywordStudyHintFull: See the picture clearly — the keyword and the meaning together. Say the word once.
studio.keywordStudyHintKeyword: Make your own picture that joins the keyword and the meaning.
studio.keywordStudyHintOwn: Find your own keyword — a word that sounds like it — and join it to the meaning in one picture.
studio.keywordOwnSub: New words, science terms, another language
studio.keywordOwnIntro: Add new words you need to learn, each with its meaning. Then make a keyword picture for each — or ask for an idea.
studio.keywordOwnRule: Add at least 2 words, each with its meaning.
studio.acronymDesc: Remember a short list in order with a word or a funny sentence made from the first letters.
studio.acronymMakeSub: 3 to 8 items — steps, parts, an order
studio.acronymIntro: Type the list in order, one item per line. Its first letters appear below — make a word or a funny sentence from them.
studio.acronymLettersHint: If they make a word, that's your acronym. If not, make a sentence below.
studio.acronymSentencePlaceholder: One word for each letter, in order
studio.acronymSentenceCheck: Each word should start with these letters, in order: {letters}
studio.acronymRule: Add between {min} and {max} items, one per line.

keywordLessonEn.l1: The Keyword method helps you learn new words — English words, science terms, words in another language.
keywordLessonEn.l2: Take a new word: frugal. It means careful not to waste money.
keywordLessonEn.l3: First, find a keyword: a word you already know that sounds like it. Frugal sounds like fruit.
keywordLessonEn.l4: Then make one picture that joins the keyword and the meaning: a fruit seller counting every coin twice before spending one.
keywordLessonEn.l5: Make the picture big, funny and moving, and say the word and its meaning once.
keywordLessonEn.l6: Later, when you hear frugal, the fruit seller comes back — counting the coins: careful not to waste money.
keywordLessonEn.l7: Science words work the same way. Photosynthesis — a photo of a plant eating sunlight.
keywordLessonEn.l8: Let's practise with three new words.

keywordLessonHi.l1: कीवर्ड मेथड से आप नए शब्द सीखते हैं — अंग्रेज़ी के शब्द, विज्ञान के शब्द, किसी दूसरी भाषा के शब्द।
keywordLessonHi.l2: एक नया अंग्रेज़ी शब्द लीजिए: frugal। इसका मतलब है सोच-समझकर खर्च करने वाला।
keywordLessonHi.l3: पहले एक कीवर्ड ढूँढिए: कोई जाना-पहचाना शब्द जो उससे मिलता-जुलता सुनाई दे। फ्रूगल — फ्रूट गल्ला।
keywordLessonHi.l4: फिर एक तस्वीर बनाइए जो कीवर्ड और मतलब को जोड़े: फल वाला अपने गल्ले का हर सिक्का दो बार गिनता है।
keywordLessonHi.l5: तस्वीर बड़ी, मज़ेदार और चलती-फिरती बनाइए, और एक बार शब्द और उसका मतलब बोलिए।
keywordLessonHi.l6: बाद में जब आप frugal सुनेंगे, तो फल वाले का गल्ला याद आएगा — और उसके साथ मतलब: सोच-समझकर खर्च करने वाला।
keywordLessonHi.l7: विज्ञान के शब्द भी ऐसे ही: Photosynthesis — फ़ोटो में एक पौधा धूप खा रहा है।
keywordLessonHi.l8: चलिए तीन नए शब्दों से अभ्यास करें।

acronymLesson.l1: Acronyms help you remember a short list in the right order.
acronymLesson.l2: Take the first letter of each item. The colours of the rainbow — violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red — become VIBGYOR.
acronymLesson.l3: If the letters don't make a word, make a funny sentence instead, one word for each letter.
acronymLesson.l4: The planets, nearest first: My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Nachos — Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
acronymLesson.l5: Say your word or sentence a few times, and link each letter back to its item.
acronymLesson.l6: Now try it on a list of your own — three to eight items.
